# WO-2026-08-12-B15-VISION-06 — Round 6: calibrated omission signal, alias-mismatch fix, Lucozade Raspberry

## Acceptance criteria

AC1 (= acceptance_property, the calibration investigation): **Use round 3/4/5's actual saved raw model
outputs** (`C:\Users\Buggly\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Fusion247PKA\65635422-06ce-4e12-8614-a5e21fb76876\scratchpad\asdair-vision-test\round{3,4,5}\run-*.json`, each with the corresponding ground-truth
file in the same folder) as your calibration corpus — real captures, real known omissions, not synthetic
data. Investigate whether a cheap, deterministic, model-free signal (per Amendment 4's own suggestion:
ink-density/line-cluster estimation per region, or another mechanism you find more reliable) can
correctly flag which of the historical regions were the ones that under-yielded, checked against what
you already know was actually missed in each of those captures. **This is a calibration exercise
against known-bad data, not a live build-and-hope** — if the signal doesn't discriminate well against
real historical data, report that plainly and do not ship it; a null result here is a legitimate
outcome, not a failure to find one.

AC2: If AC1 finds a signal that discriminates well, wire it as an ADDITIONAL follow-up trigger
(alongside the existing zero-line `silentRegions()` trigger from round 3), never replacing it. Must
remain proportionate per Amendment 4's target economic shape — a normal list stays near one call; only
regions the signal actually flags get re-inspected.

AC3: **Fix the newly-found same-region alias-mismatch bug** — round 5's live re-test found two
genuinely different real products (Lenor Outdoorable Fabric Conditioner, Febreze Fabric Freshener Spray
Lenor Spring Awakening) both read from the SAME region resolving to the SAME `matched_regular_id` in
`resolveByCatalogue.js`, causing the existing (correct, for genuine duplicates) same-region auto-collapse
to silently drop the real, distinct Febreze item. This is a catalogue/alias identity-matching defect,
not a dedup-logic defect — investigate why two genuinely different product names matched the same
regular, and fix the matching, not the collapse rule (round 3/4's collapse logic is correct for actual
duplicates; do not weaken it generally to work around this specific matching error).

AC4: **Investigate Lucozade Raspberry** — invented, at high confidence, in every live run it's been
checked (rounds 3, 4, 5), despite the household's actual regular being Lucozade ORANGE and no raspberry
variant ever appearing on the ground-truth photo. Determine whether this is a training-data-shaped model
bias (the household previously bought/mentioned a variant, or "Lucozade" alone strongly primes a common
flavour), a catalogue-grounding leak (the prompt's household context somehow suggesting it), or something
else — and fix it if a genuine pipeline-level cause is found, or report precisely why it resists a
pipeline-level fix if the cause turns out to be inherent to the model's own priors.

AC5: All touched-package tests pass with a non-zero executed count, including DB-gated tests via the
established disposable-Postgres pattern.

## Required evidence

- AC1's calibration result, stated plainly, with the actual discrimination numbers against the real
